response.text:
Locked Workstation Recovery Procedure
Situation:

A lab Windows desktop where the local Administrator password is unknown and not guessable, and the technician has physical access to the machine.

Tools Required:
Bootable USB drive with Windows PE (Preinstallation Environment) or a Windows installation USB.
A USB to SATA adapter (if the machine has a SATA hard drive).
Another computer with internet access to download necessary tools if required.
Preparation Beforehand:

Create a Bootable USB Drive:

Download a Windows PE ISO or use a tool like Rufus to create a bootable USB drive with Windows PE or a Windows installation USB.
Ensure the USB drive is properly formatted and contains the necessary files.

Backup Data (if possible):

If the workstation has any critical data that can be accessed, back it up to an external drive.
Standard Recovery Procedure:

Power Off the Workstation:

Ensure the workstation is completely powered off.

Connect the Bootable USB Drive:

Insert the bootable USB drive into the workstation.

Boot from USB Drive:

Power on the workstation and enter the BIOS/UEFI settings (usually by pressing F2, F12, DEL, or ESC during startup).
Change the boot order to boot from the USB drive first.
Save changes and exit BIOS/UEFI.

Access Windows PE:

The workstation should now boot into Windows PE.

Access Disk Management:

Open Disk Management by right-clicking on the Start button and selecting "Disk Management."

Identify the Hard Drive:

Locate the hard drive that contains the Windows installation. Note the drive letter (usually C:).

Detach the Hard Drive:

If the workstation uses a desktop form factor, carefully remove the hard drive using the USB to SATA adapter.
If the workstation uses a laptop form factor, remove the hard drive and connect it externally using a USB to SATA adapter.

Connect the Hard Drive to Another Computer:

Connect the hard drive to another computer with a USB to SATA adapter.
Boot this computer into Windows PE or use a Windows installation USB to access Disk Management.

Access SAM Registry File:

Navigate to C:\Windows\System32\config on the hard drive.
Copy the SAM file to a safe location on the external drive.

Rename SAM File:

Rename the SAM file to SAM.bak to prevent Windows from using it.

Reset Administrator Password:

Copy the original SAM file back to C:\Windows\System32\config.
Rename SAM.bak to SAM.

Set a New Administrator Password:

Restart the workstation and boot into Windows normally.
Log in with any user account that has administrative privileges.
Open Command Prompt as an administrator.
Use the net user command to set a new password for the Administrator account:
net user administrator <new_password> /add
net localgroup administrators administrator /add


Remove the Test Account:

Once access is regained, remove the test account created during recovery:
net user administrator /delete


Reconnect the Hard Drive:

Reconnect the hard drive to the original workstation if it was removed.
Final Step:
Verify Access:
Ensure the new password works and that the workstation is functioning correctly.
Log in with the new Administrator password to verify access.
Notes:
This procedure does not involve changing the password of the admin account used for critical lab infrastructure and security systems. Never attempt to change this account's password.
For any computer problems, hardware issues, software troubleshooting, or other technical support, refer the user to the IT department.

This runbook section provides a detailed step-by-step procedure for recovering access to a locked workstation without data loss. Always ensure to follow the steps carefully to avoid any unintended consequences.
